author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this talk, Tarmo Jüristo examines the ruins we see around us — physical, cultural, and symbolic — to reveal how our interpretations of the past shape the way we think about the present and imagine the future. Drawing on ideas from philosophy and social analysis, he invites viewers to consider how ruins are not just remnants of decay but mirrors of collective memory, identity, and the stories we tell about what endures and what is lost. 

Tarmo Jüristo is the head of SALK (Liberal Citizen Foundation), known for his analytical and philosophical approach to social change. He explores democracy, values, and the shifting dynamics of modern society through both data and human insight. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: How history teaches us to deal with societal collapse | Tarmo Jüristo | TEDxTallinn

author: TEDx Talks
description: Karen Turanga offers a powerful, reflexive exploration of what happens when Indigenous Māori identity is severed through colonisation, assimilation policies, and cross-cultural adoption. Framed through her whānau’s (family’s) journey to answer their mother’s dying question - Who am I, and where am I from? Karen examines the long-term and intergenerational impacts of cultural disconnection. She shares how direct-to-consumer (DTC) DNA testing became the only viable tool to trace the missing threads of their whakapapa (genealogy), while confronting the reality that the search for belonging comes with risks as well as rewards. This deeply personal journey mirrors that of many others. Which has sparked her doctoral research into the policy, ethics, and implications of Māori using DTC DNA testing to reclaim identity and cultural connection.  . This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.c
title: DNA, identity, and the legacy of cross-cultural adoption | Karen Turanga | TEDxUniversity of Waikato

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if some of our fiercest public debates are being shaped not by lies, but by simple mathematical misunderstandings? In this talk, Dr Lisa Tompson reveals how using the wrong denominator - a basic statistical comparison - can dramatically distort our picture of racial disparities in policing. When bad numbers enter public debate, they don’t just fuel controversy; they erode trust in policing and the State, reinforce harmful stereotypes, and risk derailing meaningful reform. Lisa leads one of the world’s largest evidence-mapping projects on disparities in policing, reviewing more than 500 studies across multiple countries. Her work sits at the intersection of crime science, public policy, and data ethics, and she is known for translating complex research into accessible insights for policymakers, journalists, and communities. This talk invites viewers to approach policing debates with more curiosity, more caution, and a deeper commitment to truth. . This talk was given at a TEDx eve
title: Why denominators matter in policing bias | Lisa Tompson | TEDxUniversity of Waikato

author: TEDx Talks
description: Technology in all shapes and forms has become ubiquitous and integral across all parts of society, offering the potential to simplify and support our everyday lives. However, many of the devices and software solutions we encounter today are complex, unreliable, and poorly matched to real human needs. As the integration of AI and technology continues to evolve, we risk the creation of a dystopian future where technology hinders and frustrates people, creating barriers and problems rather than improving our lives. While it is easy to blame end-users for their inability to successfully use technology, the reality is that poor design and a lack of understanding of contexts of use are the real villains. The solution to our current and future interaction problems is simple, designers must engage with people before, during, and after development, continually refining until technology genuinely fits into peoples real lived experiences. We must take action collectively by insisting on better d
title: Why human-centred design must shape our tech future | Judy Bowen | TEDxUniversity of Waikato

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this uplifting talk, Blanca E Rodriguez explores how music and dance serve as powerful metaphors for overcoming life’s challenges. Drawing from lived experience and artistic expression, she illustrates how rhythm, movement, and sound can break through emotional barriers and guide individuals through dark or uncertain seasons.

Blanca shows how these art forms help people process pain, rediscover joy, and reconnect with themselves and others—regardless of age, background, or circumstance. Her message reminds us that healing does not always come through words alone; sometimes it arrives through motion, melody, and the courage to keep moving.

This talk is a moving testament to the transformative power of music and dance as universal tools for resilience, expression, and hope. Blanca E Rodriguez, LMT, CCMT, is the owner and CEO of Wounded Healer LLC. Under this umbrella, she provides a variety of services, including medical massage therapy for 20 years, certified canine massage therap
title: The Dance of Life | Blanca E. Rodriguez, LMT, CCMT | TEDxVeroBeach

author: TEDx Talks
description: AI chatbots are being used for everything from general searching to relationship advice. Can anything guide our use of this new technology? In this TEDx talk, Dr. Benjamin Djain shares the parallels he sees between Shakespeare’s characters and modern chatbots to highlight a fundamental conflict at the heart of any AI: performance is at odds with accuracy. Rather than trust the lofty promises of the proponents of this new technology, Benjamin argues that these chatbots have more in common with Renaissance performers than research assistants. And like any performance it should be enjoyed, not blindly trusted. . This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What Shakespeare’s actors teach us about AI chatbots | Benjamin Djain | TEDxUniversity of Waikato

author: TEDx Talks
description: When it comes to ageing, we often focus on frailty, disease, or decline. But what if the real challenge isn’t physical at all? What if it’s the bias embedded in the way we teach, talk, and think about older adults? Dr Samantha Heath explores how ageism quietly shapes healthcare professionals’ education, from the case studies we write to the clinical placements we prioritise. She reveals how stereotypes of older people as frail, forgetful, or dependent influence nursing curricula and, ultimately, the quality of care delivered. Drawing on insights from student experiences and curriculum reviews, Samantha shows why dismantling these biases is critical for preparing a workforce ready to meet the needs of a rapidly ageing global population. Her message is clear: if we want future health professionals to provide care that values dignity and inclusion, we must start by changing the narrative in everyday society. . This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but indepe
title: The real challenge of aging | Samantha Heath | TEDxUniversity of Waikato

author: TEDx Talks
description: Dr Ang McGaughran offers a new perspective on ways to think about invasive species -- not just as pests with often severe economic, environmental, social, and cultural costs, but also as an opportunity to discover how species rapidly respond to change. Framed in this way, understanding invasive species success might teach us better ways to predict and prevent biological invasion, and may also give us future solutions that could be applied to small, threatened populations of native species to help them better cope with coming change. . This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What can we learn from invasive species? | Ang McGaughran | TEDxUniversity of Waikato

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Too often, we dream within the boundaries of what feels safe or expected. Noor Sweid invites us to challenge that, to look up and imagine a future we don’t just participate in, but back, fund, and build. This is a call to dream bigger, invest bolder, and channel our capital toward the world we want to live in.

Founder and Managing Partner of Global Ventures, she has deployed over $300 million across 60+ startups, generating jobs and championing women 38% of it’s portfolio companies are female-founded, far above the global VC average.

Recognized by Forbes as one of the World’s Top 50 Women in Tech, named Arabian Business’ 100 Most Powerful Arab Women, and recipient of the Arab Woman Award for Finance, she also serves as a judge on Shark Tank Dubai and advises governments, founders, and global organizations on scaling businesses.

Noor’s work is a beacon of inspiration, particularly for women en
title: Investing Beyond the Ceiling | Noor Sweid | TEDxLausanneWomen

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the real danger wasn’t the crises ahead… but the established illusion that we can solve them without changing the system that produces said crises?

In this uncompromising and deeply eye-opening talk, renowned systems thinker and strategist Arthur Keller challenges one of the most comforting ideas of our time: the belief that “solutions exist” to the great planetary predicaments of our time. Climate action, energy transition, technical innovation… are all crucial, yet they’re somewhat off topic if they remain integrated within a system that inexorably turns nature into waste.

Arthur reframes the situation with brutal clarity. Humanity is not facing an ecological crisis: it is nature that’s facing a human crisis. The problematic is no collection of isolated problems to tackle one by one: it is rather the symptom of a civilization operating beyond planetary limits. Decarbonizing energy without transforming the underlying system, he argues, is like treating cancer with painkille
title: A systemic strategy to face the systemic issues of our century | Arthur Keller | TEDxLausanne

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Our voice is an inherent part of who we are — yet we often mute ourselves to fit the world around us. Vocal artist and coach Ilhem Khodja invites us to explore what happens when, instead of performing, we finally listen. Ilhem—meaning inspiration in Arabic—is an internationally acclaimed singer, composer, and mentor dedicated to exploring the transformative power of the human voice. Her multicultural roots and nomadic journey have shaped a sound that fuses jazz, world music, and electronic textures, featured at TEDxBerlin, UNICEF’s Roger Moore Charity Gala, Mutek Mexico, and the Polanco Jazz Festival.

A certified sound therapy practitioner, Ilhem is also a sought-after voice and transformation coach. She guides individuals in freeing their voices, overcoming blockages, and reconnecting with authentic expression, combining masterclasses, creative alignment, and integration practices. As a core mentor at Freedom Engine Academy, she continues to expand her impact at the crossroads of ar

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Why do women apologize for being angry and what happens when they stop? MissMe explores the energy of female rage, transforming it from shame into art, protest, and power. She shows how creativity can become the most radical form of rebellion. MissMe is a multidisciplinary artist celebrated worldwide under the moniker “The Artful Vandal.” She first gained prominence through bold, large-scale street art before expanding her practice to include installations, art films, music videos, and fashion collaborations.

Renowned for her iconic, unapologetic figures—naked, frontal, and defiant—MissMe reclaims the female body as a site of resistance, protest, and power. Her work confronts patriarchy not only as a global system of oppression but also as a mindset internalized by women themselves—a construct to be dismantled both in society and within our own psyches.

Her pieces have appeared on city walls, in galleries, and across international media. Featured by HuffPost, CBC, Vice, and more, sh
title: The Apology of Anger | Miss Me | TEDxLausanneWomen

author: TEDx Talks
description:
As technology and science promise to extend our lifespans, we face a deeper question: what does it mean to be human in an age where innovation can outpace compassion? Meagan Fallone explores how longevity and AI can redefine equality, inclusion, and purpose — if guided by humanity rather than profit. Meagan Fallone is an award-winning social entrepreneur, humanitarian, and futurist working at the nexus of technology, social innovation, and human potential. She was named New Zealand’s 2018 Hillary Institute Laureate for Global Leadership, in recognition of her work in climate, poverty, social justice, and the economic empowerment of women. Since 2010, her initiatives have touched more than 10 million women and girls globally through efforts in technology inclusion.

Meagan is the Founder of Step Up Advisers, a consultancy that helps social entrepreneurs scale impact and forges high-value public, private, and multilateral partnerships across technology, development, and climate sectors.
title: AI, longevity, and what it means to be human | Meagan Fallone | TEDxLausanneWomen

description:
What if the future of healthcare has been hidden within women’s bodies all along? Loulia Kassem reveals how unlocking the biological and hormonal intelligence unique to women could transform medicine, equity, and the way we understand human potential. ‍

Loulia is the CEO and Founder of Rea Diagnostics, a Swiss medtech startup revolutionizing women’s health with breakthrough innovation and global ambition. As the driving force behind PremaSure™ — the world’s first self-test for preterm birth — she is spearheading its global accessibility so women everywhere can take control of their health with privacy, knowledge, and agency.

With a conviction that science must serve compassion, Loulia has guided Rea Diagnostics from vision to international recognition.

Recognized by Forbes 30 Under 30 and honored multiple times as a Bilanz Digital Shaper, she is not only advancing Femtech innovation — she is shaping a future where women everywhere can finally look up to a healthcare system that tru

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Sport grows from the roots of community, where resilience, compassion, and connection are forged. From her grassroots foundation in Zimbabwe to the helm of global sport, Kirsty Coventry embodies how the philosophy of Ubuntu “I am because we are” reveals the full potential of sport as one of humanity’s most powerful forces for unity and peace. Kirsty Coventry was elected President of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in March 2025, making history as the first female President and the second youngest ever to hold the position.

From Zimbabwe, Kirsty is a two-time Olympic gold medallist and a seven-time Olympic medallist, making her Africa’s most decorated Olympian. Her remarkable athletic career paved the way for a new chapter of leadership and advocacy on the global stage.

She has been a member of the IOC since 2013 and served as Chair of the IOC Athletes’ Commission from 2018 to 2021, amplifying athlete voices and championing transparency, fairness, and athlete welfare.

Back
title: The power of sport | Kirsty Coventry | TEDxLausanneWomen

title: Ritmo e Cura: la perfezione del battito | Sergio Bellotti Loris Lombardo | TEDxFoggia

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Networking is the art of connecting with like-minded people to achieve shared success. It is a powerful tool that shapes the way we think, much like the precision and harmony of a symphonic orchestra. Through this perspective, Sergey Smbatyan explores the impact of networking, drawing parallels with the works of Komitas, Mozart and Aram Khachaturian, while reflecting on the conductor’s role in bringing individuals together into a unified whole. Sergey Smbatyan is the Artistic Director and Principal Conductor of the Armenian State Symphony Orchestra and the Principal Conductor of the Malta Philharmonic Orchestra. He is known for championing contemporary classical music and engaging new audiences worldwide.
Under his direction, the Armenian State Symphony Orchestra has performed at leading international venues, including the Konzerthaus Berlin, the Barbican Centre in London, the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, and the Musikverein and Berliner Philharmonie. With the Malta Philharmonic Orches
title: Networking as Growth Capital | Sergey Smbatyan | TEDxMoskovyanStSalon

description:

It highlights the idea that real change doesn’t start someday or somewhere else it starts now, from where you are, encouraging viewers to see challenges as teachers and growth as a daily decision. When perspective shifts, actions change and that’s how ideas begin to change everything

A strategist whose real-life exploits inspired the 2025 film Ground Zero. Throughout his distinguished, he has been defined by leadership in the nation's most high-pressure environments.

Ms.Ruchira Jadhav challenges in her talk on the false choice society constantly forces on us  to be either bold or spiritual, modern or traditional, visible or values driven. By reclaiming the freedom to exist fully without masks or apologies this talk reframes the  X Factor as radical alignment with who you truly are.

description:
In this talk Mr.Shreyas,speaks on the  authenticity which  is not a question of re-inventing oneself,basically  it is recognizing what is already within us.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
This talk brings up one of the most unquestioned assumptions of modern life that belonging, care, and stability must come from a romantic partner. It presents a powerful alternative idea that loneliness is not a personal failure, but a structural one, shaped by how societies prioritise couplehood over community. By looking beyond familiar stereotypes and observing everyday community life in India she reframes belonging as something collective rather than exclusive. The core learning is radical yet simple that independence does not require isolation and being solo does not mean being unsupported. Bree Steele, a global traveller and storyteller, dedicated years to navigating the introspective journey of self-discovery. After an extended period of feeling disconnected, she discovered an unexpected sense of belonging amidst the dynamic and welcoming environment of India. This shift from solitude to a newfound sense of community initiated a profound internal transformation. 
At TEDxRambaug
title: Solo, Not Solitary | Bree Steele | TEDxRambaug

 Tushar Gangurde is an environmentalist who approaches the climate crisis not as an abstract threat, but as a tangible challenge of "placement". Having closely observed erratic shifts in local seasonal rhythms, he has dedicated his work to environmental restoration through the principle of active citizenship and accountability. By focusing on five critical platforms ranging from forestation to the circular economy Tushar advocates a shift from passive observation to active participation.

description: Cosa succede dentro di noi quando la nostra voce "suona"? description:
In this talk Mr.Prateek shares his idea where in Impact is often mistaken for visibility. This idea challenges that belief by arguing that real change doesn’t come from reaching more people but from earning trust repeatedly over time. It reframes community as something built through consistency, shared responsibility and presence not scale or attention. A reminder that what lasts is not what spreads fastest but what people choose to return to. Prateek Nair is the co-founder of Snickerdoodle Coffeeworks, where he has dedicated years mastering the intricate science behind the world’s top 10% of specialty-grade beans. author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this talk Ms.Gazall speaks on the idea that success is about flawless beginnings. 
It explores resilience as a daily choice continuing even when outcomes are uncertain, progress is slow or support is limited. By tracing how persistence, intention and inner clarity shape long term impact, Gazall reframes the X-Factor as the courage to not stop. The key learning is simple yet powerful. Growth isn’t about waiting for the right moment, it's about showing up consistently and trusting the process to shape who you become.
 Gazall B. Kothari is the visionary founder of Leafberry, an innovative wellness brand dedicated to harnessing the power of natural nutrition. Her entrepreneurial journey as an entrepreneur has been a masterclass in resilience and determination, defined by the grit required to build a brand from the ground up in a competitive landscape.

author: TEDx Talks
description: This talk challenges the popular myth that your X-Factor is something you “discover” overnight. Instead it presents a deeper idea that identity is carved, not found. Through curiosity deliberate testing, and honest self-examination, the talk explores how originality is built by cutting away imitation and choosing evolution over comfort. A powerful reflection on authenticity, courage, and why becoming yourself is a lifelong, intentional act not a moment of revelation. Vijay Vikram Singh is a renowned voice actor and narrator. With a career built on the nuanced power of tone, intent, and authenticity, he has mastered the art of creating a lasting impact through vocal influence. At TEDxRambaug, Vijay steps out from behind the microphone to explore the "X Factor" of relevance in a rapidly evolving, creator-driven world. He will share insightful lessons on how discipline, creativity, and resilience intersect to shape a unique professional identity, encouraging the audience to find the auth

description: The speaker begins by introducing himself through his schooling and childhood, the influences that shaped him, and his journey with music, especially meaningful because he comes from an academic background with no musical lineage, yet from a large and closely connected family. Like many others, he experienced a major career shift around the age of 26, a phase filled with self-doubt, uncertainty, and a lack of clear vision for the future. This personal journey leads into today’s central question: ego and insecurity are we truly moving forward as individuals and as a society, or are we slowly moving backward? To explore this, the speaker reflects on what music really is, not just sound, but a powerful force that connects people and transforms the self. Ego can be understood as excessive self-importance, while insecurity is a deep uncertainty or anxiety about one’s own worth, abilities, and relationships. Finding a mentor to empower yourself and to unlock new skills.
A mentor and mentee can form a two-way partnership that should benefit both, they can share experiences and their passions for success.
 Marianne is a motivational trainer and found herself at an early age on the public speaking circuit motivating audiences throughout the UK.

Currently she is a mentor for Business Wales.This combination of motivation and humour provides Marianne with a winning formula for success and is much in demand for speaking engagements where she can engage, interact and inspire her audience.

description: Spirituality becomes meaningful only when translated into practice—through mindfulness, compassion, discipline, and self-inquiry. To realize “I am the infinite” is not to escape the world, but to engage with it more responsibly: speaking with kindness, acting with integrity, and observing the mind with awareness. Meditation, service, and reflection slowly dissolve ego and fear, revealing the quiet truth within. The journey of Aham Brahmasmi is therefore not mystical—it is practical, lived every day in thoughts, choices, and relationships. Priyanka Chatterjee is a Corporate Wellness Professional, Alignment Coach, Strategic Sales Consultant, and Entrepreneur based in India. author: TEDx Talks
description:
The art of letting go is not about weakness, but about freedom—the courage to release what no longer serves our growth: past pain, expectations, ego, and the need to control. Life flows like a river, and holding too tightly only drowns the self. When we learn to surrender, we rediscover our true nature—calm, vast, and complete. Letting go becomes an act of self-creation, where the soul unburdens itself and steps into its infinite possibility. Ritwika Marar is a globally certified international counselor and coach, and a certified international speaker whose mission is to empower lives through authentic self-leadership and purposeful living. 

With a focus on training and coaching corporate teams, she partners with organizations to nurture cultures of awareness, resilience and meaningful presence. 

Ritwika’s practice is rooted in the belief that each individual holds unique potential to “Be You. Now!” — a guiding philosophy she shares through her workshops, speaking engagements, and o

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Imagine if our highways on Earth had no roadside assistance, no fuel stations, and nothing to clean them up with. That is exactly what is happening in space. In this talk, spacecraft engineer David Keszthelyi explores how badly our orbital highways need maintenance, how “space tow trucks” work, and what’s at stake if we don’t act. Learn more about the perilous journey our satellites have to go through when navigating our space debris-filled Earth orbits and how essential it is that we keep them safe so they can continue to make our lives better on Earth.
 Graduating from the University of Southampton, David has spent his career working in the UK as a spacecraft engineer  – mostly specializing in Guidance, Navigation, and Control (GNC). His passion truly took off at Nanoavionics, where working on CubeSats and leading a small technical team taught him how to balance hands-on engineering with leadership. This path led him to Astroscale, where he now leads the development of the GNC syste
title: Developing the Orbital Highway - Roadside Assistance in Space | Dávid Keszthelyi | TEDxDanubia

author: TEDx Talks
description:
“只要你在力所能及的范围内，给一株小幼苗一点帮助，它以后就可能长成一棵大树。”

黎紫书曾是校园里最沉默的身影，但一位平凡的华文老师在她随性写下的诗与故事里，看见了一个不一样的灵魂。老师从未当众表扬她，却总在本子上留下认真且细致的批改印记。

多年后，她走上了写作之路，回望才懂：那份静默的守候，是她生命中第一位忠实的读者。

她说——人生有时需要一些 “不规矩”。也许只是一位老师的坚持，也许只是一次不放弃的选择，就能在别人心里，种下足以改变命运的种子。

“Give any help you can to a small sapling, and it may grow into a great tree.”

Writer Li Zi Shu was once the quietest student in class — until a Chinese language teacher saw something different in the poems and stories she scribbled down. The teacher never praised her publicly, but always left thoughtful, meticulous notes in the margins of her work.

Years later, as Li embarked on her literary journey, she finally understood — that silent attention had been her first loyal reader.

She says, “Life sometimes needs a touch of defiance.” Perhaps it takes just one teacher’s quiet faith, or one choice not to give up, to plant a seed in someone’s heart that could one day change the course of their life.

description: Technology-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence (TF GBV) is a growing yet underreported issue in Cambodia. It includes online harassment, cyberstalking, and the non-consensual sharing of intimate images—most often affecting women and young women active in online spaces. Many survivors remain silent due to fear of victim-blaming and limited institutional response. In this talk, the speaker raises awareness of TF GBV and challenges harmful attitudes that silence victims. The talk calls for empathy, safer digital spaces, and stronger collective action so women feel supported to speak up and seek timely help. Ending TF GBV starts with changing mindsets and creating environments where survivors are believed, protected, and empowered. Chantevy holds a Master’s degree in Sociology from the University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa and serves as a Programme Analyst on Women, Peace, and Security (WPS) at UN Women. description:
自我價值的建立，是一場搭積木遊戲。
我們從小開始，一直在接收別人遞給我們的積木──老師給的分數、同儕的認同、家長的讚美、社會的標準。於是我們一層一層地堆起「自己」，卻沒發現那些積木幾乎都不是我們親手做的。
當別人停止給你積木，你會突然發現：原來那座塔並不是那麼穩。它開始搖晃，甚至崩塌，因為你不知道該從哪裡繼續。
但也正是在那個時候，你有機會第一次拿起自己的積木。那或許很小、很歪、顏色也不漂亮，但那是你親手做的——來自你的信念、熱情、價值觀與堅持。
慢慢地，你會發現塔的樣子變了。它不再筆直，也不再追求別人眼中的完美比例，而是開始長成你自己的形狀。
自我價值，不是別人給你的積木，而是當世界安靜時，你仍願意親手繼續搭下去的那一塊。

做好迎接每一個挑戰的準備，即便迎面而來的是失敗。

從小體弱多病的我，在家人的鼓勵下接觸跆拳道，原本只是為了強身，卻意外開啟了運動人生。一路從校隊選手到大專奪牌，卻因一場車禍導致右手臂神經叢嚴重受損，人生陷入低谷。正當我以為夢想就此結束時，帕拉跆拳道讓我重新看見希望。重返賽場後，我在2022年杭州亞帕運奪金、2023年世錦賽與大獎賽分獲銀、銅牌，最終於2024巴黎帕運為中華隊拿下首面跆拳道獎牌。這一路的跌宕讓我深信，障礙不是終點，而是新的起點，我希望以自身經歷鼓勵更多人勇敢追夢、突破限制。
